title: Whole Milk 1 gal

drivers.name: Price increase (5.1%)
drivers.evidence: Two weeks at $4.56 saw 195 and 119 units (vs baseline 207.6); average x0.87, noise-adjusted estimate suggests ~10% lift reduction.

drivers.name: Competitor store opening
drivers.evidence: No past equivalent; only one new entry, so effect shrunk toward 1.0; plausible downside based on category behavior.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 207.6. A 5.1% price increase to $4.56 (from $4.34) is notable, but recent data shows a price of $4.56 in 2026-09-28 and 2026-10-05 led to 195 and 119 units—below baseline—suggesting price sensitivity. The 2026-10-05 week was unusually low, possibly due to a prior promotion or stockpiling, but no such event is noted. The competitor opening across the street is a credible demand reducer. No past competitor entry is recorded, so evidence is thin. The classical model gives 1.00, but this ignores the price increase and new competition. Shrink toward 1.0 due to weak evidence. Downside spread increases slightly due to uncertainty.

PRODUCT: Whole Milk 1 gal | category Dairy | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-15 (5 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 4.56 (+5.1% vs regular price 4.34)
  planner notes: A competitor opens a store across the street this week

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 207.6 | 5%-95%: 133.4 - 290.4 | 10%-90%: 156.2 - 281.2

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-22% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
